newsitem.title: GERMANY: Henkel steps up offer for Loctite.
newsitem.headline: Henkel steps up offer for Loctite.

text.p: German consumer products group Henkel KGaA said Wednesday it was increasing its offer for the 65 percent stake it does not already own in adhesives-maker Loctite Corp.

The increase to $57.75 a share, which values the whole of Hartford, Conn.-based Loctite at $1.2 billion, was widely expected after Henkel's announcement last week that it had made an offer to the Loctite board "at a price in the area of $56."
Loctite shares closed on Wall Street at $57.875 Tuesday, marginally above the new offer price and a level suggesting a higher bid was possible.
Analysts last week said a final offer of $60 could not be ruled out.
Henkel's board said in a statement issued Wednesday that it was still seeking to hold discussions with Loctite aimed at securing a friendly takeover of the company.

Henkel's new offer, which is open until Jan. 6, is only valid if acceptances allow Henkel to increase its existing 35 percent stake past the 50 percent threshold that would give it control of Loctite.
Henkel traded 1.50 marks higher at 70.80 in an overall stronger Frankfurt bourse after the announcement.

German analysts applauded the deal as reinforcing Henkel's leadership in the world market for industrial and commercial adhesives, but there was some concern about the impact it would have on Henkel's debt.
Such a deal would double Henkel's current debt levels, which contributed to credit rating agency S&P's move to put the company on "CreditWatch" with negative implications last week.
Henkel has nonetheless said it plans to use debt to finance the proposed acquisition to avoid having to make a rights issue.

Chemical industry analysts have also noted that Loctite's earnings growth in the last four years has not been strong and that Loctite has not appeared to benefit greatly from the growth in demand for adhesives seen this year.
